mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in >60% of periods when FEDFUNDS >4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate signals labor market weakness, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns remain positive despite UNRATE increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates reduced demand in the housing market, leading to broader economic weakness and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns positive when HOUST is below 1150.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production growth signals supply chain issues, leading to decreased corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns positive despite slow INDPRO growth.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment combined with high federal funds rate indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns positive when UNRATE and FEDFUNDS are high.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns negative despite GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPI) with rising federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in late-cycle expansions.
failure_condition: SPX returns positive despite high CPI and FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing retail sales growth indicates weaker consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns positive when RSAFS growth is slow.
